summary:
Outpost Zero is a free, easy-to-play Mars base game and space learning website made for kids ages 7 to 12, families, and classrooms. No sign-up or download is needed. Players become the commander of four astronauts on Mars and try to keep everyone safe for 10 Martian days.
Instead of complicated controls, kids watch three simple bars—Life Support, Power, and Radiation Protection—and solve 16 real-life space problems. Every choice teaches a real trade-off: turning up greenhouse lights helps plants grow but uses up battery power, cleaning dust off solar panels has to wait during a dust storm, hiding in the storm shelter keeps the crew safe but pauses outdoor repairs, and radio messages to Earth take extra time.
Outpost Zero also shares real NASA Mars rover photos, daily space pictures, solar storm updates, and easy science lessons with a fun quiz, 9 medals, and a downloadable Flight Certificate—helping young learners understand how real astronauts survive beyond Earth.
details:
What We Built

We created Outpost Zero (Explore. Build. Survive. Discover.), a playful Mars survival game and space-science guide where kids lead a four-astronaut crew (Maya Chen, Mateo Silva, Priya Nair, and Leo Vance) at Jezero Crater on Mars. It opens right in any web browser, loads fast even on older phones or school computers, and still works smoothly if the internet goes out.

How It Teaches Real Space Challenges

  • Only Three Simple Bars: Kids don't get confused by too many numbers. They only need to care for Life Support (clean air, water, and food), Power (sunlight and night batteries), and Radiation Protection (safe shelter walls).
    • Greenhouse: Fix equipment, boost grow lights, clear water pipes, and pick fresh veggies.
    • Solar Power & Dust Cleaning: Brush dust off solar panels (locked when a dust storm is blowing) and turn on power-saving mode.
    • Storm Shelter: Bring the crew inside thick water-and-soil shelter walls when a solar storm hits.
    • Earth Radio Delay: Shows how far away Earth is and makes players wait through a quick 6-second countdown to send messages home.
  • Fun to Replay: Players can pick from 3 different Jezero Crater landing spots, try normal weather or Solar Storm Mode, unlock 9 Explorer Medals, check their final 100-point Mission Report, and download a personalized Flight Certificate with their name on it.

Made for Kids Ages 7 to 12

  • Simple, Friendly Words: We explain space words like sol (a Martian day), radiation, and radio delay in plain everyday language right on the screen.
  • 12 Easy Lessons & Never-Repeating Quiz: Kids can read 12 short space lessons and test themselves with a 36-question quiz that gives a fresh set of 12 different questions with mixed-up answers every time they play.
  • Classroom Friendly: Includes an easy Restart button to play again and a Full Reset button so teachers can clear the screen for the next student.

Real Space Photos & Honest Science Credits

Outpost Zero connects players to real space science from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), and always puts a clear label (LIVE NASA or FROM SAVED DATA) on every card so players know what is live today and what is saved for offline learning:

  • Live Mars Rover Photos: Real pictures sent back from the Perseverance rover at Jezero Crater.
  • Daily Space Picture & Mars Gallery: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (with a calendar picker to check different dates) plus Perseverance and Curiosity rover photos.
  • Solar Storms & Sun Flares: Real NASA space-weather updates so kids can connect actual solar storms to shielding their Mars crew.
  • Astronaut Health, Radiation, Map & Food Facts: Real NASA research on astronaut bones, muscles, sleep, and space radiation, Jezero Crater height facts, and Canadian Space Agency guides on growing food in space.
  • Note: Outpost Zero is an independent student learning project, made with respect for public space-agency guidelines and without official NASA or CSA logos.
